newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - May 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - May 7.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Wednesday's Daily Variety:

* The domestic box office broke $2 billion Sunday, setting a record pace to reach that level. Growth was led by News Corp unit Fox's first-quarter reissue of the "Star Wars" trilogy and Universal's Jim Carrey comedy "Liar Liar".
* Viacom's Paramount-based Barry London Co has purchased the romantic comedy "The It Girl" from Bo Zenga and David Freeman.

* The surprising strength of the "Ellen" coming-out episode, along with less spectacular but solid results from "Forrest Gump" and Stephen King's "The Shining," propelled Walt Disney's ABC to win the April 28-May 4 primetime Nielsens ratings.
* Polygram Filmed Entertainment has signed a first-look deal with "Evita" director Alan Parker and his Dirty Hands Productions.

* Fine Line Features, whose year at the box office was saved by the $35 million domestic performance of "Shine", dives into Cannes this week with a slate of development projects from independent filmmakers.
* "Santa's Home Page," born on America Online last Dec. 5-31, makes the jump from computers to television on ABC as "Ernie's Chistmas Special".
